lines.cap: He went in, pulled them out, and then went in again. And again.

lines.cap: Welles Crowther was twenty four. A trader on the hundred and fourth floor of the South Tower. He'd been a volunteer firefighter.
lines.say: Welles Crowther was twenty four. A trader on the hundred and fourth floor of the South Tower. He'd been a volunteer firefighter.

lines.cap: On September eleventh, 2001, a plane hit his tower. Smoke filled the seventy eighth floor.
lines.say: On September eleventh, 2001, a plane hit his tower. Smoke filled the seventy eighth floor.

lines.cap: Through the smoke, survivors heard a calm voice. Follow me. I found the stairs.
lines.say: Through the smoke, survivors heard a calm voice. Follow me. I found the stairs.

lines.cap: He carried a woman on his shoulders, led people down, then turned around, and went back up for more.
lines.say: He carried a woman on his shoulders, led people down, then turned around, and went back up for more.

lines.cap: Nobody knew his name. They only remembered the red bandana over his face.
lines.say: Nobody knew his name. They only remembered the red bandana over his face.

lines.cap: His body was found months later, next to firefighters, in the lobby. His mother learned what he did from a newspaper story.

lines.cap: The man in the red bandana. Welles Crowther.
